evidence: gpt-oss checks "p1 + p2 > T" and component totals; qwen states "place two pulses of width p1 and p2 in [0, T]"; glm checks the same JOB inequality and sorts component widths
affordance_in_statement: Let P(t; k, W) denote a rectangular pulse of width W starting at time k; formally, P(t; k, W) = 1 for t in [k, k+W]... The start times are real-valued, signals must lie in [0,T], and same-component signals must be pairwise orthogonal.
removal_suggestion: Do not state the certificate cases as independent placement problems with the phrases "even if we completely ignore...". Present the certificate definitions through an indirect witness or verification formulation, so the interval-sum tests are not handed to the solver.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes JOB as a per-item duration sum and LOAD as a per-component total-width packing test.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Rectangular pulses with real-valued starts, bounded support in [0,T], and pairwise orthogonality.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Reduces the negative-lag condition to placing the two intervals sequentially and therefore testing p1+p2 against T.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The explicit rectangular-pulse definition and the non-negative-lag correlation condition.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Tests each item's combined width and then sorts component widths to test one-dimensional packing.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Bounded support plus orthogonality of rectangular intervals.

common_affordance: The signals are rectangular intervals on a single continuous bounded line, so non-overlap is characterized solely by sums of widths.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It incorrectly accumulates p1+p2 across different items, treats all widths as one shared load, prints LOAD i instead of LOAD 1 or LOAD 2, and defaults to JOB 1 without checking the actual isolated conditions.

recommended_edit: Remove the direct interval-placement presentation and the explicit "even if we completely ignore..." decomposition; instead define JOB and LOAD through an indirect certificate-verification scenario using the same underlying constraints.
regression_risk: This may make the already-defeated deepseek-v4-flash model appear less wrong by obscuring the distinction between per-item and per-component failures.
